text:
SASRec combines item and positional embeddings with causal attention; perturbations therefore mix content, position, and transition effects ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781), [implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py)). Recommended controls: compare identical deletion sets under compact-and-right-align versus preserving original slots and explicitly excluding deleted keys/values. Keep surviving positional IDs and the final query fixed in the latter. A visible replacement token tests a different intervention; zeroing an embedding alone may leave positional information or attention access. Include count-matched random deletions, last-item-only input, and repeated prefix shuffles that fix the last observed item, sequence length, padding, and item multiset. Compare against unrestricted shuffling to expose last-item sensitivity. Last-item-fixed shuffling measures dependence on prefix arrangement conditional on that anchor; it does not establish semantic-history dependence. Removing positional embeddings alone is insufficient because multilayer causal attention retains structural order cues.

For targeted lexical-group deletions, sample within-user controls matching deletion count, interaction lag, timestamp age relative to the prediction cutoff, and preferably popularity/repetition. Match the joint age distribution, preserve the same last-item policy, report balance and unmatched cases, and repeat sampling. These are proposed identification controls, rather than established SASRec findings. Use paired validation HR@10 differences, user-bootstrap uncertainty, fixed candidates, and category macro-averages; distinguish frozen-model perturbation sensitivity from separately retrained ablations.

Treat TF-IDF title/description groups as lexical proxies until validated. Audit blinded within/between-group pairs for semantic coherence; remove boilerplate and identifiers; compare title-only, description-only, tokenization, threshold, and clustering-seed variants. Report coverage, group sizes, stability via adjusted Rand agreement, and independent training-history co-occurrence enrichment with age/popularity controls. Silhouette measures lexical geometry, not semantic validity; high-dimensional text also complicates its interpretation ([scikit-learn example](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/text/plot_document_clustering.html)). Avoid unavailable categories, ratings, or pretrained embeddings.
